messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a steady bump in 502/504s from eu-west-2 since ~06:20 UTC. Not huge but sustained.
kevin: Any pattern on client IPs or protocols?
maria: Quick correl: failure rate spikes line up with requests from IPv6-preferring CDNs and clients.
raj: Did we flip anything on the ALBs recently?
kevin: Not intentionally. Checked the ALB config: some listeners are set to dualstack and resolve AAAA for our api hostname. Target group healthchecks to targets are failing over IPv6 path. IPv4 path is fine.
maria: I ran a couple of checks from an IPv6 testbox in the same VPC:
```
$ dig AAAA api.eu.redwood.example.com +short
2a03:abcd:...::123
$ curl -6 -v https://10.0.45.12:8080/health --connect-timeout 5
*   Trying 10.0.45.12:8080...
* connect timeout after 5001ms
* Closing connection 0
```
kevin: Backend instances in that AZ don't actually have IPv6 addresses assigned on their ENIs. ALB dualstack mode tries IPv6 -> ends up hitting an unroutable path/NAT and healthcheck times out.
infra-bot: deploy 1755.12 started by kevin at 06:18 UTC :rocket:
raj: Ok — so ALB local healthchecks are attempting IPv6 to targets even though targets are IPv4-only. That's an easy misconfig but surprising we didn't catch it in canary.
sre-oncall: I'm oncall, looking now. If you need a toggle flipped I can do it.
maria: mitigation applied: toggled the target group's ip-address-type to ipv4-only for the affected target groups. Success rate returned to baseline within 60s. :thumbsup:
kevin: Repro notes for docs/incident:
- Hostname resolves to both A and AAAA.
- ALB in dualstack mode may attempt IPv6 healthchecks to targets when AAAA present.
- If targets don't have IPv6 ENIs, healthchecks time out (results in draining / 502s).

raj: Action items (short):
1) Audit all ALBs in eu-west-2 for ip-address-type / dualstack mismatch.
2) Add check in infra-lint to disallow dualstack on ALBs without node IPv6.
3) Update runbook: prefer A for healthchecks, or ensure node IPv6 assignment.
4) Capacity note: if we decide to enable node-level IPv6, NAT64 egress gateways need sizing — estimate cost impact before enabling.

kevin: I'll open a PR to the aws-alb helm chart: set `ipAddressType: ipv4` by default and a flag to enable dualstack. Also adding a diagnostic script snippet to detect AAAA->target mismatch.
maria: Reminder: some stable customers on modern mobile networks prefer IPv6; turning off dualstack for public frontends will affect client econ/latency slightly. We'll schedule a brief maintenance to do a region-wide fix after a whitelist test.
sre-oncall: Creating incident ticket INF-2026-134 and assigning to network team. I'll post updates in this thread.
kevin: +1. I'll paste the diagnostic output and the PR link once open.
raj: Also add a note to the capacity/cost doc: NAT64 requires persistent gateways per AZ; include GPU fleet impact if we push more egress through central NAT64 nodes (could increase inter-AZ traffic).
maria: Thanks — good catch. We'll follow up with a postmortem and checklist to prevent dualstack mismatch next time. :spiral_note_pad:
